newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks firm at opening, scale back gains.
newsitem.headline: French stocks firm at opening, scale back gains.

text.p: French shares continued to climb at the opening on Tuesday, with a jump of 0.34 percent on the CAC-40 index before retreating slightly.
Traders said the market feels firm and the next targets on the upside are 2,294/96, then 2,303/05 on the CAC. Support is seen on the downside at 2,268/70 and 2,257/59.
Brokers point to Wall Street's 1.17 percent rush up overnight and an all-time high in London as positive for Paris.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 2.08 points or 0.09 percent at 2,279.22 at 0912 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,282 from 2,277 on Monday's close.
Concerns about the franc later pushed down the CAC index. The French currency fell below 3.3900 against the mark as a truckers' strike sparked fears of widening labour unrest.

Alcatel Alsthom falls 0.94 percent to 465.70 francs. Liberation reported that chairman Serge Tchuruk was preparing a new bid for electronics firm Thomson SA if Lagardere Groupe's offer missed the December 31 deadline. A broker said the report raised concerns. The European Commission and French Privatisation Commission have to approve the sale.
Carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen off 1.12 percent to 617 francs. "The stocks has had a very good runup," said one broker. Renault was up 0.33 percent at 120.40.
A drop in October car sales was well-flagged.
Sanofi adds 1.6 percent to 456.20. The stock has put on more than 40 percent since the start of the year, boosted by merger speculation with Rhone-Poulenc.

Cie de Suez firms one percent to 223.30. Financial holding companies Suez and Paribas up 0.47 percent at 363.80, are seen as potential candidates for consolidation, following the Axa-UAP insurance merger.
